_about: Building blocks for generating light expedition stories. Derived from the official scripted expeditions (The New Age, Into The Wild, Tales of Old Gravehold) and Legacy campaign cards. Placeholders: {mage}, {mages}, {nemesis}, {ally}, {place}, {quest_giver}, {treasure}, {npc}.

style.voice: Second person plural ('you'), past or present tense, as on the Legacy cards.
style.length: Prologue 2 short paragraphs; each battle intro 1-2 paragraphs; each conclusion 1-2 paragraphs; epilogue 1 paragraph ending on a hook.
rules: Show the Nameless through signs before it appears (see nemeses.signs).
Every victory closes the breach and reveals a clue that leads to the next battle.
Frame treasure as artifacts found, recovered, or crafted from Nameless remains — never as loot from nowhere.
A mage added to the Barracks should be met in the story (rescued, found, or volunteering).
Give each selected mage at least one line of dialogue in their voice (see characters.traits and their mat quotes).
Respect canon: do not kill or redeem canon characters outside an explicit 'what if' expedition.
End the epilogue on a door left open: 'The work of a breach mage is never done.'
canon_phrases: the burnt-air smell of an opening breach

beats.purpose: A summons or alarm sets a goal and stakes.
patterns: A panicked messenger bursts in during your report: {omen}.
An expedition has not returned; it carried {stakes}.

beats.purpose: Travel through a setting, notice the signs, ambush.
patterns: The trail gives way to {terrain}. {sign}. Then silence — and {nemesis} is upon you.

beats.purpose: Close the breach, take stock, find the clue and the reward.
patterns: As {nemesis} falls you force the breach closed. Among the remains you find {treasure}, and {clue}.
{ally} stumbles out of hiding — alive. They join you.

beats.purpose: Survive, retreat, return stronger (Expedition rule: refight the battle).
patterns: Blackness strobes at the edge of your vision — then {rescuer} is standing over you. {nemesis} withdraws, wounded but alive.
You retreat into the dark. It will be waiting.

beats.purpose: Report to the quest giver, reveal a twist, open the next door.
patterns: You report to {quest_giver}. They thank you — but {twist}.
Suddenly the doors of the hall slam open.

arc.escalation: Battle 1 nemeses are scouts/lieutenants/experiments; Battle 2-3 reveal the plot; Battle 4 is the source; Battle 5 (if used) is the mastermind or the thing behind the source.

rewards_by_battle.1: five level-1 treasures: personal artifacts left by fallen teammates or recovered from the first lair
rewards_by_battle.2: three level-2 treasures: group relics (city artifacts, ancient objects) found at a ritual site or archive
rewards_by_battle.3: five level-3 treasures: masterwork equipment crafted from Nameless remains or found in a forge/bunker
rewards_by_battle.4: level-4 treasures plus a new mage and supplies: the source's hoard and a rescued legend

era_bridges._about: Canon ways to mix mages or nemeses from different eras in one expedition.

bridges.text: Time is wrong in the Void: some stay the same age for centuries, others age decades in an instant.
Yan Magda's cadre wandered the spiral of worlds and arrived out of time.
Nook's time experiments tangle past and future (The Anomaly).
The Fountain of Souls reconstitutes the aether of the fallen — old enemies and friends can return.
Gravehold's archives record every Nameless ever fought; an old enemy's kin can reappear (Wayward One → The Wanderer).
Nameless are never truly gone: their survivors and fragments grow anew.

twists: someone saw the insignia of Xaxos on a fleeing robe
the Nameless you fought was once human
the artifacts were stolen from the city's own vault
one of the rescued now carries Void essence inside them
the creature you killed was someone's family
the signs you followed had been left for you to find
